name: Basic Bessemer lining
summary: Thomas and Gilchrist lined the Bessemer converter with a basic material that removed phosphorus, letting Europe's abundant phosphorus-rich iron ores make good steel.
description: Thomas and Gilchrist modified the converter lining to remove phosphorus during Bessemer steelmaking.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: The ordinary Bessemer process could not remove phosphorus, so steel could not be made from the phosphoric ores common in Europe.

date.basis: Blaenavon experiments from 1877, reported success in March 1878, subsequent Middlesbrough refinement in 1879.

events.statement: Thomas and Gilchrist modified the converter lining to remove phosphorus during Bessemer steelmaking.
events.caveats: Heritage account does not specify lining recipe or removal chemistry; those details are withheld.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 1: Experiments in Blaenavon; cached text lines 45–60
evidence.supports: Experimental sequence, lining change and dates.

date.label: by 1883
date.basis: The 1883 government survey records use already underway in the six named countries; it does not give the date when use began.

events.statement: By publication of the 1883 census survey, the basic-lined Thomas–Gilchrist process was reported in industrial use in Britain, France, Germany, Austria, Belgium and Russia.
events.population: Industrial steelmakers in the specific European countries named by Swank
events.caveats: The survey observes usage by publication, not its first date or universal adoption; the source gives no plant-by-plant audit.

evidence.locator: printed p. 127 / PDF p. 24, first full paragraph
evidence.supports: The process and basic converter lining are identified, followed by explicit in-use reporting.

This is the earliest supported record currently established here, not certification of absolute priority.

community_entry.community: Industrial steelmakers in the specific European countries named by Swank
community_entry.rationale: Actual outside industrial use outranks the makers’ 1877–1879 experiments. The 1883 publication provides a conservative upper bound, not an invented 1880 observation.
community_entry.caveats: The survey observes usage by publication, not its first date or universal adoption; the source gives no plant-by-plant audit.

links.statement: Thomas and Gilchrist changed the Bessemer converter lining to address phosphorus in the feedstock.
links.alternatives: Use suitable low-phosphorus feedstock or another refining route.
links.caveats: The source gives a historical sequence, not quantified removal performance.
links.timing: The base converter precedes the documented modifications by two decades.
